SEC22A-01.note: Head is 'wild oat seeds' (plural); 'as well as ...' is parenthetical and does not count, and 'Nobody sows... sprout on their own' rules out the passive. 'germinates' tempts readers who agree with 'bindweed'; 'are germinated' is grammatical in isolation, so voice is settled by meaning.

SEC22A-02.note: 'A number of' takes a plural verb, and the present results ('emit', 'are no smaller') call for the present perfect. 'has adapted' is the trap for readers who treat 'A number' as singular; 'were adapting' clashes with the present-tense results.

SEC22A-03.note: 'Hydroponics' is a singular field name despite the -s, and the passage is in the present ('can cut', 'add'). 'are practiced' traps readers misled by the -s ending; 'was practiced' has the right number but the wrong tense.

SEC22A-04.convention: simple present used as habitual/narrative present in a 'when' clause
SEC22A-04.note: The singular head 'spheroid' (absolute phrase 'its outer cells...' set off by commas) rules out A and C. The progressive fits best because growth is under way when the drug is added and then halts; the simple 'proliferates ... when they add' can read as growth CAUSED by the drug, but as a narrative present it is grammatically defensible, so tense is settled by meaning rather than by any convention.
SEC22A-04.drop_reason: Under 'when the researchers add', the simple present 'proliferates' is still defensible as a habitual or narrative present (the default form in a lab-procedure description). Only a semantic inference from the next sentence ('growth halts') favours the progressive, so the item is not exclusive under convention alone.

SEC22A-05.note: The verb belongs to 'the bird' inside the relative clause 'that the bird ___', so it is singular and active, with the gap as its object. 'were depositing' tempts readers who agree with 'seeds'; both passives ('the bird was/were deposited') are garbled once read.

SEC22A-06.note: Head 'units' is plural and the units receive the screening, so the verb is passive. 'has been screened' traps readers agreeing with 'donor' or 'antibody'; 'have screened' wrongly makes the units the screeners.

SEC22A-07.note: The subject is 'a single plant' (singular), and the parallel 'the more ... secrete' sets the simple present. 'attract' traps readers agreeing with 'bees'; 'has attracted' breaks the tense parallel.

SEC22A-08.note: 'which' refers to the plural 'samplers', and the ongoing present ('give', 'continue') calls for the present perfect progressive. 'were operating' has the right number but the wrong tense; the singular options trap readers agreeing with 'county'.

SEC22B-01.note: Head 'piezometers' is plural, and the narrative is in the past ('filled', 'opened'). 'was recording' traps readers agreeing with 'technician' or 'boat'; 'are recording' has the right number but the wrong tense.

SEC22B-02.note: Head 'wires' is plural, and 'by hydrogen' requires the passive. The long interrupting 'because' clause ending in 'coating has worn away' and the singular 'cable'/'bridge' pull readers toward 'is being attacked'.

SEC22B-03.note: 'A slab' is singular, and the next sentence ('remains attached', 'widens each summer') requires an ongoing process. 'has detached' agrees but contradicts the slab still being attached; the plural options trap readers agreeing with 'trails'.

SEC22B-04.note: 'alignment' is singular despite the compound 'between X and Y', and the finished past project ('advanced', 'broke through') rules out the present perfect. 'were checked' traps readers counting two headings; 'has been checked' traps on tense.

SEC22B-05.note: After 'nor' the clause inverts; the subject is the singular 'instrument', and the base form 'measure' needs 'does', not 'has'. 'have the' mirrors the earlier 'have never sampled' (parallel attraction), and 'do the' fails on number.

SEC22B-06.note: 'The latter' refers to the wrought-iron rails (plural), and the closed historical period ('cracked', 'by the end of that period') requires the simple past. 'was costlier' traps readers treating 'The latter' as singular; 'have been costlier' has the wrong tense.

SEC22B-07.note: The subject is 'One such icy moon' (singular), with the parenthetical 'spacecraft measurements suggest'; the direct object 'jets' requires the active voice. The plural options trap readers who agree with 'measurements'; 'has been ejected' leaves 'jets' without a verb to govern it.

SEC22B-08.note: Head 'Attempts' is plural, and a static present describes what a paper contains. 'is documented' traps readers agreeing with 'astronomer' or 'brightness'; the progressive wrongly implies documentation still under way.

SEC22C-01.note: Head 'questionnaire' is singular (the plural possessive 'statisticians'' is the attractor), and 'from the season it was printed' requires the present perfect. 'is indispensable' agrees but cannot carry the 'from ...' span.

SEC22C-02.note: The verb is compound with 'transcribed', sharing the plural subject 'teachers'. The registries closed two winters ago, so the progressive 'have been contributing' (ongoing) is ruled out. The singular options trap readers agreeing with 'museum', 'diary' or 'schoolmistress'.

SEC22C-03.note: Within 'whose ___', the subject is the plural 'scripts', and the story is set in the past ('wrote', 'memorized'). 'was being passed' traps readers agreeing with 'playwright'; 'are being passed' has the wrong tense.

SEC22C-04.note: 'which' refers to the singular 'varnish' (or the stripping as a whole), not 'owners', and the 'Whenever' habitual frame requires the simple present. 'are logged' traps readers agreeing with 'owners'; 'has been logged' traps on tense.

SEC22C-05.note: Whether 'that' refers to the boys or the priest is settled only by context: the priest wears his everyday cassock and the boys are costumed, so the verb is plural. The grandmothers dress them, so it is passive. 'is dressed' is the strong trap because 'priest' sits next to 'that'.

SEC22C-06.note: Head 'script' is singular; the 'unlike those of ... dramas' interrupter and the plural possessive 'puppeteers'' are attractors. 'in each of the seasons that followed' requires the present perfect.

SEC22C-07.note: Head 'claim' is singular (the attractors are 'monks' and 'charters'), and 'spread by itself ... without any pamphlet' requires the intransitive active. 'was being circulated' agrees and is grammatical, so it falls only on meaning.

SEC22C-08.note: The fronted participial phrase inverts the clause, so the subject is the plural 'initials' after the verb; the present-tense frame ('disagree', 'read') rules out 'were'. The singular 'master'/'panel' and the singular-looking gerund phrase make 'is' attractive.

tells: Every option set is a 2x2 grid of number (singular/plural) by a second axis (tense, aspect or voice). Exactly two options agree in number, so the number decision always halves the set, and the remaining pair is always settled by tense or voice from the surrounding sentences. A test-taker who learns the grid can drop the two options sharing the number of the nearest noun before the blank: that noun mismatches the key in A-01, A-05, A-06, A-07, B-01, B-02, B-03, B-07, B-08, C-01, C-03, C-04, C-06, C-07 and C-08 (an attractor in most items), though not universally (A-02, A-04).

The batch is close to monotype: 22 of 24 items test subject-verb agreement plus tense or voice on a main verb (B-05 and C-08 are inverted auxiliary/copula variants). No punctuation, boundary or modifier items appear, so on a real module the batch would read as one subskill.

Where voice is the second axis (A-01, C-07), a nearby sentence explicitly says the action happens on its own ('Nobody sows or waters them', 'spread by itself'), which telegraphs the active option. A-04, B-03 and C-02 likewise put a later clause that names the aspect ('halts', 'remains attached', 'stopped accepting').
I found no letter-position tell: by my answers the keys are A 6, B 6, C 6, D 6, and singular and plural keys are 12 each.

singular head preceded by plural possessive attractor, present perfect with since-span
intransitive active versus passive, telegraphed by 'on their own'/'by itself' sentence
plural head with prepositional attractors requiring plural passive
progressive versus perfect decided by a later sentence about current state
relative clause inside subject, past/present passive on plural noun
